messages.author: b35f414539b34a6c
messages.subject: Procustes aligning faces
parts:
Hey all,

So I'm working with faces and I was thinking that when i Procrustes align my data i'd want to take the symmetrical component of variation to use in future analyses because faces have object symmetry. Am i right in thinking that increases my statistical power because it cuts the shape space in half?

And if this is true, rather than using gpagen(), am i right in thinking i'd use bilat.symmetry() to align them, and giving the function the paired landmarks i could take the $sym.shape element from the aligned data and use that as the symmetrical component? 

Because when i try this on my 688 observation dataset (I have 8 observations each of 86 people: 2 camera types, 2 photos of the same face from each camera type, and each photo digitised twice) I put in the information on which observations come from the same person. When it gives me the $sym.shape output its collapsed across my 86 participants. Ideally as i want to examine the 688 observations, is ok in this case to leave out the 'individual' and 'replicates' arguments? I assume you'd only want to include these anyway if you're using the bilat.symmetry function to do a procrustes anova?

Thanks,

Richie

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Procustes aligning faces
parts:
Dear Richie,

bilat.symmetry is the correct function to use here, and yes, proceed with the $sym.shape 3D array. 

You are certainly able to leave those elements out if you wish, it is your study. But the question you have to ask yourself is why you are not averaging your replicates? Performing any analysis after the GPA on all 688 observations will be confounded by pseduoreplication.

Emma
